newsitem.title: USA: Fifth trainer charged in U.S. Army base sex probe.
newsitem.headline: Fifth trainer charged in U.S. Army base sex probe.

text.p: A fifth trainer at the U.S. Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground was charged in a sexual misconduct probe at the base, and a soldier accused earlier was discharged in lieu of a court martial, the Army said Tuesday.

The proving ground said in a statement that a drill instructor, Sgt. William Jones, was charged with fraternisation, being drunk on duty and indecent assault. The charges involved six female trainees and one female civilian.
Jones, 34, is a 16-year veteran of the Army.

He is the fifth trainer to be charged in a sexual misconduct scandal at the base, which houses an ordnance training school. The scandal erupted in November and has led to an Army-wide investigation of sexual harrassment.
Jones faces a maximum punishment of six months in jail as well as fines, a rank reduction and a bad-conduct discharge if convicted.
The proving ground also said Sgt. Theron Brown, who was charged Jan. 16 with sodomy, adultery and other violations, had requested and received "a discharge in lieu of court martial."

Proving ground spokesman George Mercer said the continuing probe at the base is investigating allegations implicating about 20 additional soldiers. Two of the soldiers already charged face accusations of rape. The others face lesser charges.
Mercer said regulations prevented the disclosure of the nature of Brown's discharge.
In addition, the proving ground said the court martial trial of Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson, one of the two soldiers facing rape charges, had been rescheduled to April 8 from February.
